REGIS REPORT

15 August 2025

Jollibee (JFC PM) reported 1H net profit of P5.6bn, down just a shade (1%) vs the prior year. Revenues grew 15% while operating profit was up 18% but items below EBIT clearly led to net income being virtually unchanged YoY. These operating results appear in line with expectations of the Street and Regis. For 2Q alone, revenues rose 15% while operating profit was up 19%.

 

Among the highlights of 2Q were a mild deceleration in SSSG for the domestic business (+6.4% vs +8.5% in 1Q) and an improvement for the international business (+4.1% vs +0.7%), which was attributed to an improvement in China. The Jollibee brand operations also appear to be leading growth with SSSG at +9% in North America.

 

The company is holding a briefing later today and we expect to glean more from that.

 

+++

 

1H25 recurring profit of Alliance Global (AGI PM) grew 20% to P10.6bn, on our estimates, slightly ahead of consensus forecast. Earnings of its three major subsidiaries, Megaworld (MEG PM), Emperador (EMI PM), and Travellers, all showed sequential improvements in the second quarter. Profits at Golden Arches (GADC), meanwhile, appear to be flattish YoY. More below.

 

+++

 

On the hot topic of the day, the results of Digiplus Interactive (PLUS PM) are likely to fuel more backlash from politicians with the Senate hearings on online gambling underway.

 

1H25 net profit of PLUS reached P8.4bn which is 61% higher YoY, albeit slightly behind consensus forecast. 2Q25 revenue grew 7% QoQ (+31% YoY), slower than the 23% growth of the industry. Thus, despite spending a huge amount on advertising and promotions, the company’s market share fell from 45% in 1Q25 to 39% in 2Q25.

 

Meanwhile, investors will likely be more focused on the news that the BSP ordered banks and e-wallets to remove links that redirect users to online gambling platforms within 48 hours. However, consumers should still be able to access gambling platforms directly and use then their e-wallets for funding. Thus, there will likely be a decline in online gambling but by no means is this a death knell for the industry.  

 

There have been a number of proposed policy changes by members of the Executive and Congress. Here’s a quick guide:

 

 

+++

 

While Nickel Asia’s (NIKL PM) 1H25 recurring profit of P1.3bn (+16% YoY) appears short of our estimates, a deeper look shows that the miss came from elevated non-cash expenses and a higher tax rate. Revenues and EBITDA otherwise are tracking ahead of forecasts, after ASPs surprisingly surged 51% YoY in 2Q25 and 40% YoY in 1H.  At yesterday’s briefing, management sounded upbeat on the near-to medium-term prospects of its nickel mining unit, indicating that Indonesia’s ore production limits will likely benefit Philippine nickel miners for a prolonged period. 

 

+++

 

Vehicle sales for the month of July declined amid work disruptions caused by heavy rains, as well as the imposition of excise taxes on pickup trucks.  CAMPI reported a 3% YoY drop in industry-wide sales (ex-BYD) while sales of Toyota Motor Philippines also slipped by 2% YoY.

 

+++

 

Data from the Mexican port authority indicated that volumes at ICTSI’s (ICT PM) Mexico port (CMSA) fell 12% YoY in July, following a 14% YoY decline in June. While operations remain hampered by logistics disruptions, the impact on earnings was likely cushioned by storage revenues during this period.

CONSUMER
JFC 1H25 profit down 1% YoY to P5.6bn—in line

1H25 operating profit up 18% YoY to P10.8bn

JFC’s 1H25 net profit was slightly down 1% YoY to P5.6bn, which is in line with REGIS and consensus expectations. Core operations appear broadly in line as 1H consolidated revenues rose 15% while operating profit was 18% higher YoY. For 2Q25 alone, top line grew 15% YoY to P77.6bn and operating profit increased 19% YoY to P6.0bn. Consolidated SSSG was steady at 5.5% in 2Q25, unchanged from the previous quarter.

 

Jollibee brand continues to drive the overall business

The domestic segment’s 2Q systemwide sales (SWS) grew 11.3% to P65.2bn, boosted by new store openings in the quarter as SSSG mildly decelerated to +6.4% from +8.5%. The Jollibee brand (+7.0%) and Mang Inasal (+12.0%) were the primary drivers of growth in SSS in 2Q. The slight deceleration was due to Chowking SSSG slowing down to 2.3% from 6.2% in 1Q.

 

The international segment in 2Q saw SWS climb 32.6% to P49.3bn given a YoY boost from Compose Coffee, which contributed to 6.8% of total SWS. In terms of SSSG, the int'l segment improved to 4.1% from 0.7%, driven by a reversal from China. The segment continued to see good performance from the Jollibee brand internationally, which posted strong SSSG (e.g., Jollibee NA +9.4%, Jollibee Other Asia +10.0%).

 

China improves, Smashburger deteriorates

China saw a turnaround in 2Q, arresting five consecutive quarters of SSS decline with SSSG up 3.9%. However, Smashburger remains challenged seeing SSS decline 9.9%, even worse than the 8.0% drop in the previous quarter.

 

More after the briefing at 4pm today, register here.

 

 

CONGLOS
Alliance Global 1H25 headline profit rises 60%
  • Alliance Global 1H25 headline profit grew 60% to P14.0bn
  • Removing non-recurring gains in 1Q25 (from the de-consolidation of Golden Arches), we estimate that recurring profit would have risen 20% to P10.6bn, slightly ahead of consensus forecast 
  • The company said that excluding GADC (which is still 49% owned), 2Q25 profit would have been P5.3bn, vs 2Q25 headline profit of P5.6bn
    • This implies that AGI’s share in GADC profit was c. P300mn – flat YoY
  • 2Q25 GGR of Travellers fell 5% QoQ (and 17% YoY) to P7.5bn
    • Management said that hold rates of VIP were stable QoQ but volume was soft
    • The win rate and volume of mass were generally stable
  • However, 2Q25 EBITDA rose 19% QoQ and 25% YoY to P2.5bn, due to lower promotional allowances and other expenses
  • 2Q25 top line of Emperador rose 14% QoQ but fell 3% YoY to P15.0bn
    • The strong momentum in brandy sales (+11% YoY to P9.8bn) was dragged down by the continued decline in whisky (-23% YoY to P5.2bn)
    • Brandy comprised 65% of total revenue in 2Q25
  • EBITDA for 2Q fell 5% to P3.1bn given lower revenue and gross profit
    • Brandy's margins saw a boost from product mix on the strength of the premium priced products
    • Whisky margins however, deteriorated due to product mix given softness in the sales of single-malt whisky

GAMING
BSP orders supervised institutions to remove links to online gambling within 48 hours
  • The BSP issued a directive to all BSP-supervised Institutions, including e-wallets, to remove links providing in-app gambling access from their payment apps and websites within 48 hours
  • Suspended in-app gambling access includes any product/service/feature that redirects an account holder to a gaming/gambling site
  • While links that redirect to online gambling platforms in the e-wallets will be removed, e-wallets can likely still be used to fund online gambling
MINING
Nickel Asia: Core profits bounce in 2Q25 on sustained strength in ore prices

Higher non-cash costs, taxes offset revenue/EBITDA beat

NIKL reported 1H25 profits of P2.1bn, up 88%. Removing the FX adjustment relating to the divestment of Coral Bay HPAL, we estimate recurring profit stood at P1.3bn, up 16% YoY. The results fell short of our estimates due to larger-than-expected non-cash costs and a higher tax rate. Otherwise, 1H25 revenues of P11.8bn (+27%) and EBITDA of P4.6bn (+53%) outperformed, after considering seasonal factors. Note that NIKL’s production typically peaks in 2Q/3Q.

 

Mining unit rebounds on better weather

After weather-related disruptions in 1Q, the mining unit staged a strong rebound in 2Q25. Revenues jumped 42% YoY to P8.3bn, as stronger ASPs (+51% YoY) more than offset a 3% drop in sales volumes. Consolidated EBITDA surged 273% QoQ and 88% YoY to P3.6bn.

 

Solar facility suffers from soft WESM prices but company on track to double capacity

Weak WESM prices offset the 8% YoY improvement in GWH sales volumes at its solar facilities, causing 1H25 EBITDA to drop 12% YoY to P460mn. Management said that it has already fully contracted its existing 172MW capacity, as well as the upcoming 120MW solar facility slated for commercial operations in 4Q25. It expects another batch of ~290MW of new solar facilities to come online within the next year or so, with management planning to lock in prices by participating in GEAP.

 

Upbeat outlook

Management remains upbeat on nickel prices, citing the Indonesian government’s commitment to support ore prices. While nickel ore prices (1.4%) have softened a bit to US$38/MT from the peak of US$42/MT in 2Q25, policies that limit ore production under RKAB (Indonesia’s production quota) will likely benefit Philippine nickel ore exporters for a prolonged period (4-5 years).

 

Valuations

At 7x FY25E PER, NIKL trades at a wide discount to Indonesian nickel miners (14x). The company has maintained a good dividend track record, with its FY25A DPS of P0.11/sh (50% of 2024A profits) offering a yield of 4%.  

 

 

CONGLOS
Heavy rains, tax on pickup trucks dampen vehicle sales (ex-BYD) in July
  • CAMPI reported vehicle sales fell 2.6% YoY, 5.4% MoM to 38,295 units
    • CAMPI cited weather-related disruptions, but we suspect the imposition of excise taxes on pickup trucks last July 1 may have also contributed to the weak sales (Toyota raised prices for the Hilux by 10-20%)
    • Note that CAMPI’s data does not capture BYD sales
    • Brings YT-July car sales to 269,207 units, up 1.4% YoY
    • Assuming BYD’s market share of ~5%, we estimate industry car sales would have likely grown ~6% YoY
  • Sales of electrified vehicles (EVs) stood at 2,707 units in July, down 11% MoM
    • Brings 7M25 EV sales to 16,195 units, accounting for 6% of overall car sales
  • Toyota Motor Philippines (TMP) sold 18,058 units in July, down 1.8% YoY, 8% MoM
    • This brings 7M25 sales to 129,334 units, up 5.4% YoY
    • To reach TMP’s sales target of 235k units (+8%), sales should average 21k units per month for the rest of the year
    • To reach REGIS’ sale forecast of 231k units (+6%), sales should average 20k units per month for the rest of the year
  • TMP is a 51%-owned unit of GT Capital (GTCAP PM) and accounts for 31% of NAV (24% of gross asset value) and 35% of 1H25 net profit
  • GTCAP is trading at a 38% discount to its market-based NAV of P1,123/sh and 5x FY25E PER

 

TRANSPORT
Volumes at ICTSI’s Mexico port down 12% YoY in July as logistics disruptions persist
  • Data from Mexico’s port authority showed that container volumes at ICTSI’s port, Contecon Manzanillo (CMSA) fell 12% YoY to 110k units in July
    • Decline is still due to the prolonged effect of the labor strike in May, which disrupted operations across Manzanillo
    • Ex-CMSA, combined volumes at other ports in Manzanillo dropped by 1% in July
    • Note that revenues would have likely been steady due to higher storage revenues
  • Brings CMSA’s cumulative 7M25 volumes to 851k TEUs, up 3% YoY and trailing our forecast of 1.69mn TEUs (+16% YoY)
    • To reach our forecast, volumes for the rest of the year would have to average 167k TEUs per month
    • The port’s capacity today is 1.7mn TEUs (~142k TEUs per month) and this capacity will increase to “over 2mn TEUs” (~168-175k TEUs per month) by year-end (new berth will be completed by Aug/Sep 2025)
    • We estimate CMSA accounts for 12% of consolidated volumes, 21% of revenues, and 25% of group EBITDA
  • ICTSI trades at 9x Regis FY25E EV/EBITDA (10.4x consensus), in line with peer median but below peer average of 12x
